header.name: Theories of Deep Learning
header.description: Deep Learning (under the broader umbrella of Machine Learning) nowadays is a popular approach that allows computers to learn attributes from data. The aim is to enhance our understanding in terms of a hierarchy of concepts, where each such concept comprises of simpler ones. Alongside the proliferating application of these techniques for image, audio or time-series data, practitioners have developed a good understanding of the properties that make these deep nets effective. There are now a number of theories being developed to give a more formal mathematical understanding to accompany these observations; this course will explore some of these varying perspectives. The course is finally assessed by individual projects instead of an End-semister Exam. Students will be given assignments which will include mathematically involved pen and paper questions, along with few computational experiments. This course is focused on theoretical aspects of deep learning. Computational experiments help explore the theory, and are a valuable skill. You will have significant scope to select a topic of interest to you, but there are some restrictions; details to follow.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to explain why deep learning leads to more expressive representation models.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to identify tools from Random Matrix/Information theory and apply them to achieve training accelation/generalization in very deep models.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to analyse and explain the training dynamics of deep nets using various visualization techniques.

lecture_topics: Introduction to theoretical aspects in Deep Learining (DL)
Data classes and curse of dimentionality
DL through lens of Matrix Factorization (MF)
Supervised and Unsupervised learning via MF
Input domain partitions and random paths
DL through lense of Random Matrix Theory (RTM)
Evolution for signal variances and covariances in infinite depth DNN
Discussion: Extended results for advanced architectures based on CNN and ResNets
DL through lense of Information Theory
Spectral Visualization: Generalization error in DNNs
Discussion: Adversiarial examples and why they are universal
